title: Minimum Speed to Arrive on Time
summary: Given a floating-point number hour representing the total time to reach the office, and an integer array dist of train distances, find the minimum integer speed (in km/h) for all trains to ensure you arrive on time.
statement: Given a floating-point number hour representing the total time to reach the office, and an integer array dist of train distances, find the minimum integer speed (in km/h) for all trains to ensure you arrive on time. If impossible, return -1. Note that each train departs only at integer hours, necessitating potential waiting periods between rides. Tests ensure the solution does not exceed 10^7 and hour has at most two decimal places.
constraints: hour has at most two decimal places.
All non-final train times round up to the next integer hour; return -1 if speed 10000000 is insufficient.
hints: Feasibility is monotonic: any speed above a feasible speed is also feasible.
Round every non-final trip upward, but keep the final trip fractional.
Binary-search speeds 1 through 10000000 using hundredths to avoid boundary rounding errors.
The predicate exactly models departure waits, and binary search returns the first feasible integer in a monotonic range.
editorial: The predicate exactly models departure waits, and binary search returns the first feasible integer in a monotonic range.

tests.explanation: At speed one the trips take 1, 3, and 2 hours, meeting the six-hour limit.
Speed three gives waits of 1 and 1 hours plus 2/3 hour, so it is minimal.
